reasons: Deviation classification is correct: unspecified Materials default to Type II, i.e. IBM/third parties hold all right, title and interest in work product created during the Service performance period, and the Type II licence back is limited to use/execute/reproduce/display/perform/distribute 'within Customer's Enterprise only' with no right to modify or sublicense — this fails the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for our business) on material terms, so it is not mere upgrading of an acceptable fallback.

Redline is directionally right and appropriately scoped: it flips only the default (unspecified Materials created during the Service performance period become Type I/Customer-owned), broadens the Type II licence to add perpetual, modification, derivative works and sublicensing for Customer's business, and leaves IBM's ownership of pre-existing materials and its platform components untouched — consistent with the rule's 'Vendor keeping ownership of its platform is fine'.

New subsection (e) supplies the missing Customer Data/Content ownership statement using the agreement's own defined terms (Content, Customer Components, Services Recipients) and grants IBM only the limited rights needed to deliver the Services, matching the redline guidance to add a Customer Data ownership sentence without creating joint ownership.
Changed-character ratios (0.43 / 0.47) are justified here because the rule requires reversing the default ownership direction and rewriting the licence grant; no smaller edit reaches the fallback.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice with the [Playbook] prefix, and correctly explains both changes; rationale correctly notes no assignment of Customer IP/data to IBM and no joint ownership, so no walk-away issue is overstated.
